preview: the tool had to fit a multi-node platform rather than a local-only demonstration. each retained component had to answer a clear need in ingestion, storage, processing, governance, quality, orchestration, or observability. the stack had to remain technically consistent across services and interfaces. the selected technologies had to support reproducibility, monitoring, and service separation. the final choices had to

title: Apache Kafka
preview: [!htbp] Apache Kafka acts as the ingestion backbone between dataset producers and downstream storage services . it structures raw data transport through explicit topics and allows controlled replay when a stage must be re-executed. Kafka makes ingestion observable, modular, and better aligned with modern event-driven data engineering practices than direct one-shot file transfers.

title: Hadoop HDFS
preview: [!htbp] HDFS stores the bronze data generated from Kafka consumption . it offers distributed persistence, replication, and strong compatibility with the surrounding Hadoop and Spark ecosystem. HDFS gives the platform a real distributed storage layer instead of a local folder-based approximation, which strengthens the realism of the deployment.

title: Apache Spark
preview: [!htbp] Spark is the main distributed compute engine used for transformation and loading tasks . it integrates naturally with HDFS, Iceberg, and the cluster deployment model, while remaining academically recognizable as a standard big-data processing engine. Spark gives the platform real parallel computation capabilities and serves as the backbone for both the raw-to-curated flow and the lakehouse loading logic.

title: Trino
preview: [!htbp] Trino exposes the analytical tables through an SQL query interface . it separates interactive exploration from heavy transformation workloads and provides a clean querying layer for validation and analysis. Trino improves usability, supports manual verification through SQL clients, and reinforces the idea that a lakehouse must serve both engineering and analytical access needs.

Parquet remains an efficient columnar analytical format that naturally complements curated transformation outputs . dbt turns transformations into governed assets rather than ad hoc scri
preview2: pts, which makes the platform easier to explain, validate, and maintain.

title: Great Expectations
preview: [!htbp] Great Expectations formalizes validation checks on important data assets . it helps transform quality from an implicit assumption into a visible engineering control. the tool provides auditable validation artifacts and strengthens the trustworthiness of the resulting data products.

title: Apache Airflow
preview: [!htbp] Airflow orchestrates the ordered execution of reset, ingestion, transformation, validation, and lakehouse readiness workflows . it provides explicit DAG-based orchestration, retries, scheduling, and operational visibility. Airflow transforms the platform from a collection of scripts into a controlled execution system with traceable runs and clear dependencies.

title: Docker
preview: [!htbp] Docker isolates services and makes the deployment reproducible across the control plane and VM nodes . it simplifies service packaging, environment consistency, and deployment repetition. containerization makes the platform easier to rebuild, demonstrate, and stabilize, which is especially important in an academic distributed setup.
